findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable network paths and increases attack surface.

The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and snapshots unencrypted at rest. Compromise or unauthorized access to underlying storage or snapshots could expose database contents.

The EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. A compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would permit broad control and data access across these AWS services.

findings.issue_category: database credential exposed in user data
findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user_data and written to a local configuration file. User data can be retrieved by processes or principals with access to the instance or its metadata/service configuration, exposing the database credential.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This gives the database unrestricted outbound network access, increasing exposure if the database host is compromised.
